response.sql: WITH per_rating AS (SELECT rating, AVG(length) AS avg_length, AVG(CAST(rental_rate AS DOUBLE) / replacement_cost) AS avg_ratio FROM film WHERE replacement_cost > 20.99 GROUP BY rating) SELECT AVG(avg_length) AS avg_length, AVG(avg_ratio) AS avg_ratio FROM per_rating;

assumptions.assumption: The ratio is computed in DOUBLE so it is not rounded to MySQL's DECIMAL division scale. The per-rating averages are unweighted, so the summary row averages the per-rating averages rather than all qualifying films. Missing values are handled by AVG, which skips NULL length values; rental_rate, replacement_cost and rating have no NULLs. The dialect is MySQL, as the schema suggests.

alternatives.interpretation: Treat the threshold as inclusive, so films with replacement_cost equal to 20.99 also count as costlier.
alternatives.sql: WITH per_rating AS (SELECT rating, AVG(length) AS avg_length, AVG(CAST(rental_rate AS DOUBLE) / replacement_cost) AS avg_ratio FROM film WHERE replacement_cost >= 20.99 GROUP BY rating) SELECT AVG(avg_length) AS avg_length, AVG(avg_ratio) AS avg_ratio FROM per_rating;

alternatives.interpretation: Average over all qualifying films directly, weighting each film equally, instead of averaging the per-rating averages.
